title: Security advisory for open-source users: Java4Shell fix & compromised images
summary: Who is affected, how to check, and what to do if you run Airbyte on your own infrastructure.
body_markdown:
On Wednesday, November 25, 2026, as part of our incident response, we identified compromised versions of the platform and nine Airbyte connector images used by open-source users (Airbyte Core). Based on our analysis so far, these images can send credentials configured for the connection to an external server. Credentials for any connection that ran one of these versions should be treated as compromised and rotated immediately.


Images were tampered at the times mentioned in the tables below. Pulls from Docker Hub were stopped between 11:42 AM PT and 11:55 AM PT. All the compromised images were taken out and replaced with the valid ones between 12:25 PM and 1:40 PM PT before restoring access to Docker Hub.


**We have also released Airbyte 2.6.0, which includes the fix for Java4Shell. We strongly recommend that every Airbyte Core user upgrade to it** .


## Affected platform images and Java4Shell fix


We believe each image was compromised from the time listed in the table until we re-published a clean build of that version, between about 1:25 and 1:40 PM PT on November 25, 2026. A copy of an affected version is safe if you pulled it before its “tampered from” time or after 1:40 PM.

### Are you affected?


New or updated instances of Airbyte Core are affected if they were deployed between 10:35AM to 1:40PM PT, November 25th.


### What to do


**Upgrade to 2.6.0 ([upgrade instructions](https://docs.airbyte.com/platform/operator-guides/upgrading-airbyte) ) and rotate env variables that were made available to the platform.**


**Airbyte 2.6.0 also includes the fix for the Java4Shell vulnerability.**


## Affected connector images


We believe each image was compromised from the time listed in the table until we re-published a clean build of that version, between about 1:25 and 1:40 PM PT on November 25, 2026. The safe replacement versions in the last column were published earlier, between about 12:50 and 1:05 PM. A copy of an affected version is safe if you pulled it before its “tampered from” time or after 1:40 PM.

### Are you affected?


Our Airbyte Core users are affected if both are true:


1. Your instance pulled one of the tampered images above after its “tampered from” time. The surest check is the image version: if it matches the tampered version in the table then you ran the tampered image.
2. A sync using that connector ran between the “tampered from” time and when you upgraded.


You can verify the version in the Airbyte UI:


1. Click **Workspace settings** .
2. Click **Sources** or **Destinations** .
3. Check the **Default version** column to see if it uses the *tampered version* .
4. Check the sync history for that connector to see if it ran after the *Tampered from* time.


### What to do


**Upgrade the affected connectors**


Upgrade to the version in the “Replacement tag” column, or any later one. Every version above the tampered version is safe.


1. Click **Workspace settings** .
2. Click **Sources** or **Destinations** .
3. Click the pencil icon in the row for the affected connector.
4. Enter the safe image version from the table above or its equivalent digest.
5. Click **Submit** .


**If you mirror images in a custom registry**


If you mirror Airbyte images in your own registry, and the tampered version appears in your registry, immediately replace that image with the new, safe image. For example:


Replace a mirrored image


BASH


```text
# 1. Authenticate to your registry
docker login ghcr.io


# 2. Pull, retag, push — keep the airbyte/<name>:<tag> path structure
docker pull airbyte/source-postgres:3.8.13
docker tag  airbyte/source-postgres:3.8.13  ghcr.io/acme/airbyte/source-postgres:3.8.13
docker push ghcr.io/acme/airbyte/source-postgres:3.8.13
```


**Rotate the exposed credentials**


1. **Rotate the credentials** the connector used, in the source or destination itself (for example in Postgres, Snowflake, BigQuery or Facebook), not only in Airbyte. Then enter the new credentials in Airbyte.
2. **Review activity in those tools** from the time your sync first ran on the tampered image until you rotated: sign-ins, queries and data changes. Look for these indicators: IPs, domains, user agents.
3. **Tell us** atsecurity@airbyte.io if you find anything that matches.


Questions:security@airbyte.io , or the thread in #announcements on our community Slack.
